# Strict affine-contact rigidity of the R4 facet martingale

This note sharpens the finite R4 convex-order certificate. It does not
assert that a perturbed cap profile has the old marginals or retains its
old efficiency bound. It proves an exact necessary rigidity whenever the
old base marginals are retained, independently of which transport is used.

## 1. A discrete convexity discriminator

Use the high and low point lists H,L in
`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/r4_facet_martingale_exact_slab_recovery.json`, with physical base coordinates
z=(z1,z2) and a third tier coordinate s. There are27 high and66 low points.
For a convex function b on D4, define

    Delta(b)=9 sum_(l in L)b(z_l)-22 sum_(h in H)b(z_h).        (1)

Then Delta(b)>=0 by the exact martingale's Jensen inequality. Moreover

    Delta(b)=0 if and only if b is affine on D4.                (2)

Equivalently, if h_z is the number of high tiers at base z, (1) is

    Delta(b)=sum_(z in P)(27-31h_z)b(z).

It annihilates every affine function, as follows either from the exact
marginal moments or directly from the displayed complete lists.

## 2. Equality propagates across fourteen actual martingale supports

Every positive transport row expresses its high base as a strictly
positive convex combination of the target bases. Since Delta is the sum
of its nonnegative Jensen gaps, equality in (1) makes b affine on each
row's target hull, including the source base. The elementary Jensen-equality
proof is given in Section2 of the common-facet contact-rigidity source:
a positive barycentric equality forces affine interpolation throughout
that convex hull.

The following fourteen rows suffice to propagate one affine function to
ALL31 bases. Indices are the zero-based high-row indices in the exact JSON.
For the first row choose the three listed noncollinear points to determine
an affine function. Each later row shares the listed full affine basis
with previously covered rows; its own Jensen equality therefore extends
that same function to its newly listed points. Rows with two basis points
are collinear, and two points determine the restriction to that line.

| row | old affine basis (initial basis for row0) | new points |
|---|---|---|
|0|(-4,-4),(-3,-3),(-2,-1)|(-4,-4),(-3,-3),(-2,-2),(-2,-1),(-1,1),(0,3),(0,4)|
|1|(-4,-4),(-3,-3),(-2,-1)|(-1,-1),(-1,2),(0,2)|
|2|(-4,-4),(-1,2)|(-3,-2),(-2,0)|
|7|(-4,-4),(-2,-2),(0,2)|(-1,0),(0,1)|
|9|(-2,-1),(-1,-1),(-1,0)|(0,0)|
|16|(-1,-1),(0,0),(0,1)|(1,0)|
|17|(0,0),(0,3),(1,0)|(1,1),(2,0),(3,0)|
|18|(0,1),(0,4),(1,0)|(2,1)|
|20|(0,3),(2,0),(2,1)|(1,2),(1,3),(3,1),(4,0)|
|24|(0,4),(1,3)|(2,2)|
|5|(-4,-4),(-2,-2),(2,0)|(-1,-2),(1,-1)|
|6|(-3,-3),(-2,-2),(-1,-2)|(-2,-3)|
|10|(-4,-4),(-2,-3)|(0,-2),(2,-1)|
|13|(-3,-3),(-1,-2),(-1,-1)|(0,-1)|

Every row/basis/new-point entry is checked from the actual positive
rational support, not from an approximate coupling. In particular the
union contains the three outer vertices of D4. The shared affine
interpolations therefore show b agrees with one affine function on P.
To show equality throughout D4, one of the positive Jensen rows contains
an interior base, and b is already affine on all its support hull; however
an even simpler argument uses b(0) and the three outer vertices. The
origin is their strictly positive barycenter and its value equals their
affine interpolation. Jensen equality then forces b affine on all D4.
This proves (2). Conversely any affine function makes every martingale
Jensen gap vanish.

## 3. What this says about common-facet perturbation

Suppose the old high and low base/tier marginals are retained while actual
points are moved to a common facet lower graph lambda_i=b_i(z), with b_i
convex. Any physical martingale between these moved marginals, whether
or not it uses the original144-edge support, must preserve the affine
coordinate lambda_i in TOTAL expectation. It therefore requires
Delta(b_i)=0. By (2), the lower support graph b_i must be affine.

Applying the corresponding relabeled facet argument to all three normals
would force all three lower support-offset functions affine. That returns
to homothetic simplex fibers on an affine center graph, where the favorable
symmetry-selected circuit is already proved to pay Gamma.

The fixed-marginal premise is essential. In a general deformation, facet
areas, profile transition positions, and high/low weights may change.
The theorem does not assert that low efficiency itself supplies the old
marginals, nor that every possible new convex-order certificate has the
same strictness. It gives a concrete affine-contact obstruction to
transporting the existing certificate through a nonaffine support motion.
